items.text: Greetings Sleepers,

The new Update 1.4 is officially available. This update introduces two new locations and new Landsraad missions. In addition, the Water Wars DLC launches today, adding Water Shipper–themed building pieces and cosmetics.

Once a Harkonnen tech hub, the Wind Pass is now controlled by the Water Shippers and serves as a key center of Arrakis’ water trade. This location also brings five new Landsraad missions with unique rewards.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/b3fbd41d55839755eb7dc65b8a8704b0be87816c.gif"]
A scalable new Testing Station where players will face Dr. Jalanta, a devious new boss with her own set of unique mechanics, hidden deep within her secret laboratory.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/2234d986ea3e68aa86ca809ccd76fa8d080887e9.gif"]

Players can now self‑host Dune: Awakening battlegroups on their own machines and customize their experience. Hosts can adjust various settings through configuration files to tailor server behavior. Among a myriad of other settings you can tweak, you can also adjust the balance of PvE and PvP, even making your server fully PvE or PvE if you prefer. This feature is still an early iteration and will continue to evolve.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/5f94d8625c69d7d621aea95ee42ef2e00c5ef97c.gif"]
Approaching the one‑year anniversary, the game has received more than 15 updates — including the recent change making PvP fully optional, giving players full control over how they experience Arrakis.

Update 1.4 is not a Chapter update. It’s a smaller release while the team continues work on major upcoming content. Beyond the recently discussed Polar Cap map, even more is in development: new features, new content, and the continuation of the main story.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/66f224034d1fadd91c828238adf8e7372ad84665.gif"]

To celebrate the launch of Update 1.4, Dune: Awakening is 40% off on Steam, bringing the price below $30 / €30. Funcom is also launching the Community Challenge: Secrets of the Water Shippers, challenging players to complete The Old Quarry as many times as possible. items.text: Well met Sleepers,

Chapter 3 is our biggest update yet, reshaping the endgame and opening new paths of progression across Arrakis and responding to the biggest requests from our community. In addition, a new DLC is out now, Raiders of the Broken Lands. There is a lot packed into this update so we will walk you through the highlights below, but you can find the full patch notes here.

The update is comprised of two main parts. The first is the free update which everyone who owns Dune: Awakening has access to immediately. The second is the DLC Raiders of the Broken Lands also available immediately to anyone who bought the Season pass, the Deluxe or the Ultimate Editions at no additional cost. Otherwise, you can get access to it for $9.99, or buy the full season pass for $24.99.

At the heart of Chapter 3 is a redesigned Landsraad that gives players more to do, more rewards, and deeper customization in playstyle. Endgame progression will still be focused around the Landsraad, but this has been completely rebuilt. Now, you will be able to select Missions, a new activity type, which will earn them Faction Ranks, Great House Standing and Specialization XP. Let’s go through these one by one:

Faction Ranks – This has been expanded to include additional levels. At the end of the ladder, the Faction leader you’ve chosen will give you a brand-new special mission to culminate your rise in the ranks.

Great House Standing – Like before, the Landsraad is decided by earning favor with Great Houses. But going forward, you will select a mission first and decide which Great House you will earn standing with.
Specialization XP – Every mission will give you a new type of XP that will level up one of the 5 new specializations. We’ll get into this mechanic next.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/d8e3795353078b3e02e06081a7ce788a89996ab9.png"]

We are introducing 5 new specialization tracks that let you deeper refine how you play: Crafting, Gathering, Exploration, Combat and Sabotage. These can be progressed with Specialization XP. Doing this will unlock unique traits which will offer significant bonuses, like increasing headshot damage, inventory slots or unlock entire technologies like Augmentation.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/a5fded7c26232bdb60cc6d4823d8609693fc6d25.png"]

Augments can be added to Unique Tier 6 weapons and Armor to increase their power even further. There are tons of new augments to discover and craft. The schematics for these can be found in the new Testing Stations and they can be added to gear in the new Augmentation Station. Unlocking Augmentation requires progression in the Crafting Specialization. Once gear has been augmented though, items can be shared and traded.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/242ec1192510bee183dab2780ac6c953ccdc1796.png"]

To house these new missions, 10 new overland map locations have been added, as well as new locations to support the new chapter of the story and new Faction Rank contracts. In addition, the overland map has received some visual changes and we have removed the Fuel and Water requirements.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/3d8938b02b887f0d27bee7331fade8c84d9674b1.png"]
5 of the new locations are dedicated to repeatable challenges. These are the setting for the new Landsraad Missions which will progress your Specialization, Faction Rank and Great House Standing.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/216193ce11d0979d4a0c55482d724f7e9ed96194.gif"]

You can also find 5 new Repeatable Testing Stations. These all feature a new type of boss fight which will require players to develop new tactics. In addition, these can be repeated and the difficulty can be scaled. Higher difficulty yields higher rewards.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/85a0abb5f655ac7f37a44a3906a210c53f82b1eb.gif"]
The story continues with Chapter 3. Fight through the Neo Carthag Duelling ring, and team up with an unexpected ally as you dig deeper into the mystery of your origin.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/cd2248fd50e251e41fffdaa8308caa1f817259eb.png"]
Two new weapon types have been added: The Pyrocket and the Dual-Wielded Knives. The Rapier has also been completely reworked with new moves, attacks and defenses.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/24740ca25bb4e20ace7c918e3f62329e684d42bf.gif"]
Base Taxes have been fully removed. Base upkeep is now simpler, clearer, and far less disruptive to play.

Power requirements are still active to avoid building locations from being blocked indefinitely by inactive players, but with the removal of taxes and the Base Reconstruction Tool, base upkeep should be greatly simplified.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/f4135c6c9d385fefe7cf332d178029b072d02bfa.png"]

For those who will be returning to Arrakis after an extended absence, we’re introducing Return Packages. These are designed to help returning players get back into the action quickly, without needing to rebuild from scratch and can be accessed via the escape menu.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/7332e33b839199cea233ee966081b2a8f8e17cef.gif"]

We have also polished the layout of the Deep Desert expanding the shield wall across the whole of the southern section of the map. And we’ve added more ramps to make the endless dunes easier to reach with ground vehicles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/eeae47a4a94ce4771bdcf85522b07f9434c711ac.gif"]

Included in the mechanics mentioned above are a series of rewards offering much more cosmetic variety to Dune: Awakening. These include new Vehicle variants, new double garage doors for larger vehicles, as well as many armor and weapon variants as rewards or in-game vendor items. You’ll also be able to apply swatches you own to base utilities allowing you to further customize the look of your base. Twitch Drops from Chapters 1 and 2 can now be purchased at the relevant vendor in Arrakeen and Harko Village, meaning you can get the entire Observer Building Set in-game.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/4de14d3fa3c8aed2d794ccc0b42034f3434361d4.gif"]

Raiders of the Broken Lands offers a list of cosmetic items. One of the most common requests is more items to build with so this DLC includes building pieces and decorations, some weapon and armor variants and more. See the full list below:
74 Smuggler Building Pieces: Build a practical yet comfortable base on Arrakis with these Smuggler Building Pieces.

items.text: Greetings, Sleepers!
[p align="start"]Today marks the release of Patch 1.2.40.0, which introduces an exciting new feature long requested by our community: character transfers!

[p align="start"]You can now transfer your character, inventory, backed-up bases and vehicles, and bank contents (including your Solari) to a new Sietch and World. You can start the transfer process via the Server Browser or the in-game System Menu.

[p align="start"]You will need a transfer token to initiate the transfer. You start with one, which replenishes automatically seven days after you have used it. However, before doing so, you should prepare accordingly to ensure that you bring your most important possessions with you.
[p align="start"]Before transferring your character, we recommend completing the following steps:
Make sure that you back up your base using the Base Reconstruction Tool. Also, remember that you can store up to three bases in the tool.
If you transfer without backing up your base(s), they will be left behind!
Similarly, back up your vehicles with the Vehicle Backup Tool.

For larger vehicles that don’t fit in the VBT, you can disassemble them with the Welding Torch and store the parts in your bank or base storage. This makes it doubly important that you remember to back up your base!
If you exceed the VBT vehicle limit, you can also disassemble any extra vehicles in your fleet and store their parts!
The cargo container is counted as a vehicle and will not be backed up by the Base Reconstruction Tool.
Make sure to store any other valuables in your inventory and bank, as their contents will be transferred along with your character.
Finally, ensure that your character is in Hagga Basin before initiating the transfer. You won't be able to start the process if your character isn't on this map.

[p align="start"]Once you initiate your character transfer, follow the on-screen instructions and prepare to meet your new friends (and foes) in your chosen Sietch and World. And remember, we are still working on Server Migrations, which will be included in a future patch at some point after the release of Chapter 3. In the meantime, use Character Transfers to find your new spot in Arrakis.
Read the full patch notes here. Please note that the full patch notes are only available in English.

notes.title: Chapter 3 Free Update: A New Endgame — Built With Our Community

items.text: Chapter 3 is shaped by thousands of conversations, suggestions, and bits of feedback from across the Dune: Awakening community. One of the clearest messages we heard was the desire for more meaningful progression and choice – including PvE players - after reaching tier 6. This update sets up the framework to do this, expanding late-game play with deeper choices, shared goals, and more ways for every type of player to continue growing. We’ve rebuilt the Landsraad system to give you more ways to progress and earn meaningful rewards—whether you’re playing solo or teaming up with friends.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/e98c61ee3492f7baf53c2ef032145b6181439a6b.jpg"]

Faction ranks have been extended and we’re introducing two progression loops in the form of Specialization and Augmentations which work together. On top of that, the overland map has been expanded with several new locations, including unique repeatable testing stations featuring challenging boss encounters with scaling difficulty and increasingly valuable loot.

These include a rework of the rapier, and the introduction of two weapons: the Pyrocket and Dual Blades. releases.displayName: New Patch Now Live with Vehicle Recovery System and More!

items.text: Greetings Sleepers,
A new patch has just gone live, introducing the vehicle recovery system! Today’s patch also brings a number of significant improvements, including to the Deep Desert looting experience.

Your feedback and support continue to motivate the team as they work on shaping Arrakis and improving your time there. Take a look at the highlights of today’s patch below, and check out the full patch notes here.

Your vehicle backup tool now has a new function – Recovery Mode. With this, you can restore any destroyed vehicle at the cost of Solari and the maximum durability of that vehicle. Items stored in the vehicle’s inventory cannot be recovered.

Keep in mind that destroyed vehicles are only recoverable for a limited time (currently 72 hours). Whether it was the victim of a sandstorm, sandworm, or anything else, any vehicle can be restored. Please note that only vehicles lost after today's patch will be recoverable.
The construction tool now features a ‘Replace' mode that can be used to replace building pieces with other compatible pieces. This allows you to quickly upgrade your bases to new sets.
The view distance of vehicles has been drastically increased (2 km) across all of Arrakis.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/67b198cc38d4bd31e420376c482bc08d777e95f6.gif"]

Loot in PvP areas is now instanced, bringing it in alignment with other areas in the game. Every player will now get their own personal loot in the PvP areas of the Deep Desert. This ensures that you will always be rewarded for successfully clearing an area with loot chests.
PvP loot has been rebalanced to fit this new experience. The loot in PvP areas still has increased drops compared to PvE areas.

We have implemented a new loot structure for schematics in the Deep Desert. Schematics are no longer ever off rotation, meaning they can all be acquired at any time. Schematics are still tied to a certain location like a Testing Station or shipwreck (higher drops in PvP areas). The result is that for a single shipwreck for example, the loot pool is far larger, but individually, the schematics have a lower drop chance.
The goal of this is to make all areas in the Deep Desert more consistently rewarding to explore and loot, while also making some rarer items somewhat more available.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/7c9813d4e181aecca22012b4332d3446e1a6e543.gif"]
The banks of Arrakis have been patched to store far more. The previous restrictions were too harsh, and there were not enough ways to safeguard your hard-earned resources.
Bank slots have increased from 25 to 500.
Bank inventory volume has increased from 1500 to 30000.

releases.displayName: Regarding the Dune Man Building Pieces

items.text: First, big thanks to everyone who jumped into Chapter 2 and the Lost Harvest DLC yesterday and who took the time to share your thoughts with us.

We realize that our communication around the contents of the DLC has not been clear enough. The Lost Harvest DLC has a variety of content, with the focus being on the new side story and the Treadwheel, but the way the Dune Man building pieces were communicated created expectations that it would be a full building set rather than what was our intention: four new pieces to supplement the base game building sets.

We understand the disappointment some of you have shared, and to rectify that, we will work on creating more Dune Man building pieces that we’ll make available to all owners of the Lost Harvest DLC. We’re looking at adding around 15 more pieces and we aim to have these available late September or early October.
Some of you were asking if we were planning on releasing additional Dune Man building pieces via Twitch Drops. No, that was never the plan. Those campaigns have their own exclusive rewards.

While we’re on the topic of Twitch Drops, we can also share that we plan to make all (including past) Twitch Drops obtainable in the game and we’ll provide more details about that when ready. As with many other games, Twitch Drops are important for us to support the creator ecosystem and give the game more visibility on the Twitch platform. But, while these are free rewards available to everyone, we understand not everyone wants to or have the time to watch live streams and we want to make sure those people also get access to these items in-game sometime after the Twitch Drops campaign concludes.
Once again, thank you for spending time with Chapter 2 and the Lost Harvest DLC, and please keep sharing your thoughts with us. We’ll keep you updated on all the above.

releases.displayName: Chapter 2 Free Update and The Lost Harvest DLC

items.text: Greetings Sleepers,

Change is coming to Arrakis. We’re excited to announce that our Chapter 2 free update and The Lost Harvest DLC, priced at $12.99, will release on September 10th, as revealed in the Into the Infinite Showcase at Gamescom!
UPDATE: We have moved the date forward to September 9!
Today, we will cover what you can expect in the free Chapter 2 Update, the Lost Harvest DLC, as well as a few other events to look out for in the near future.
Get a taste of the update and DLC in our announcement trailer!

Our update plan for Dune: Awakening is structured into free major content updates in the form of Books and Chapters, and paid content in the form of DLCs and Expansions. Generally, Chapter Updates will be released in parallel with DLCs.

Chapter 2 will be our first major content update. Embark on the next chapter of the main story following the sinister revelations at the end of Chapter 1. Explore new locations, meet new and familiar faces, delve deeper into the nature of your origins, and unravel a web that stretches into the darkest corners of the Imperium.
Alongside the continuation of the story, Chapter 2 brings several new contracts, new dynamic encounters, new archetype armors, character re-customization, and more.

The Lost Harvest is a paid DLC with a complete standalone storyline. A carryall transporting a Miner’s Guild spice harvester has been shot out of the sky, and its cargo could change everything. Your job is to find it.

The DLC also includes several unique cosmetics, including a brand-new vehicle, the Treadwheel, complete with its own unique animations and tier upgrades. The vehicle and other cosmetics provide no material benefit over its base game counterpart.
Other cosmetics include several armor and weapon skins, and the Dune Man building set, letting you build bases in the style of those pragmatic and weathered workers of Arrakis.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/fdbebf4d0d3758fdf0f4e72bf05e5dd9bb91feb4.jpg"]

The DLC is available for $12.99 and is included in the Season Pass ($24.99), which includes The Lost Harvest DLC and two more major DLCs. The Season Pass is already included in both the Deluxe and Ultimate Edition. We look forward to sharing more details on the DLC.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/78e1de69fa65b18c4e43adbaa4bed172e8798479.jpg"]

Earlier today we launched our Free Trial, letting anyone taste the spice of Arrakis for free, for 10 hours, until August 24th. Free Trial characters are unable to play with those who own the game, but they will keep their character’s progress and backpack contents if they purchase the game.

The only inaccessible areas are Arrakeen, Harko Village, and the Deep Desert. The entire Hagga Basin is free to explore, with all its varied biomes. Advance through the story, build a base, a vehicle, and explore the vast deserts. In almost every respect, the Free Trial gives you access to everything the full game has to offer.

items.text: Greetings Sleepers,

A new hotfix went live today, bringing changes to the Deep Desert, ornithopters, visiting other Sietches, and more! The full patch notes have already been released, but we’d like to highlight some of the changes here.
If the download for the hotfix hasn’t appeared for you, please restart your Steam client.

As discussed in detail in the message from our Creative Director, this is the first iteration of the changes to the balance between PvE and PvP in the Deep Desert. As of right now, the PvE area has been expanded to include the southern half of the Deep Desert map. Pockets of PvP will remain within the new PvE zone for Control Points and Shipwrecks.

With this change, we have also rebalanced resources in the Deep Desert somewhat, with density increasing the further north you go, including spice. Loot is overall more valuable and plentiful in the northmost PvP zones. Having said that, it’s important to note that the highest tier of resources are still available in the bottom half of the Deep Desert.
We will continue monitoring how this plays out and continue iterating when and if needed.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42849822/43cd155746ec1c07f6f7db1ef4a86c3fa7562d5c.jpg"]

Equipping a Rocket Launcher Module now decreases the top speed of Scout Ornithopters by 20% and 10% for Assault Ornithopters. We have more changes planned but this is in line with the goal of encouraging meaningful decisions about how you outfit your vehicles and choosing whether you want to be aggressive or not in PvP zones.

We have removed restrictions when visiting other sietches. Before, you could visit other sietches but you couldn’t claim land. Now, any player can go to any sietch in their World and claim land wherever they want (the max number of sub-fief consoles (3) remains unchanged).
Additional Fixes
In this hotfix, we have also brought a number of fixes and improvements addressing stability, combat, user interface, and more.
Thank you all for your continued feedback and bug reports, it’s very helpful! Check out the full patch notes to see all the changes.

This means that players who have no interest in PvP should be able to find what they want without engaging in PvP. Imperial Testing Stations, caves, and so forth found in this area are thus now PvE.

Control Points and Shipwrecks will, however, continue to be PvP throughout the entire map, which means you will find localized pockets of PvP within the PvE section still. Similar to how Shipwrecks are PvP in Hagga Basin.

The lower half of the Deep Desert now offers PvE loot that is balanced toward shared loot and PvE activities. You may find better loot in the more dangerous PvP area located further north on the map. In the PvE area, for example, each player gets their own loot and can expect to receive one schematic. In the PvP area, loot is distributed on a "first come, first served" basis, with higher quantities of everything. Players can expect to find 2–6 schematics there, which are among the rarest.
Plasteel plates can only be found in PvP zones. This line was inaccurate, since Plasteel plates can be obtained from crashing ships.

The respawn time of Titanium and Stravidium has increased from 30 to 45 minutes.
